tagline: The nation's largest retailer of used vehicles.
hero_kpi_rationale: CarMax is the largest retailer of used vehicles in the United States. Its retail used vehicle unit sales volume is a key indicator of its performance and market position.

kpis.name: Retail Used Vehicle Sales
kpis.explanation: Total number of used vehicles sold directly to consumers.
kpis.description: Represents the core of CarMax's business, measuring its ability to sell cars to individual customers.
kpis.signal: Stable sales volume despite a competitive market.

kpis.name: Wholesale Unit Sales
kpis.explanation: Total number of vehicles sold at auction or to other dealerships.
kpis.description: Indicates CarMax's performance in selling vehicles to automotive industry professionals.
kpis.signal: Sustained wholesale activity, diversifying sales channels.

kpis.name: Net Sales and Operating Revenues
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from vehicle sales and related services.
kpis.description: A comprehensive measure of the company's economic activity.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in revenue, reflecting market dynamics.

kpis.name: Gross Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit realized after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: An indicator of direct profitability from vehicle sales.
kpis.signal: Slight decrease in gross profit, impacted by acquisition costs.

kpis.name: CAF Income
kpis.explanation: Profit generated by internal automotive financing operations.
kpis.description: Measures the financial contribution of CarMax's customer credit offerings.
kpis.signal: Stable financing income, supporting overall profitability.

kpis.name: Used Gross Profit Per Unit
kpis.explanation: Average profit generated per used vehicle sold.
kpis.description: A key indicator of pricing efficiency and per-unit cost management.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in per-unit gross profit, requiring tighter acquisition cost management.

kpis.name: SG&A as % of Gross Profit
kpis.explanation: Ratio of operating expenses to gross profit.
kpis.description: Measures operational efficiency by evaluating operating costs relative to generated profits.
kpis.signal: Increase in SG&A expenses, requiring cost optimization.

kpis.name: Net Earnings per Diluted Share
kpis.explanation: Net profit attributable to each outstanding common share.
kpis.description: A key indicator of profitability for shareholders.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in earnings per share, affecting shareholder valuation.

kpis.name: Digitally Enabled Transactions
kpis.explanation: Percentage of transactions where the customer uses digital tools or completes at least one step of the purchase process online.
kpis.description: Measures the integration of digital platforms into the customer purchase journey, including omnichannel and fully online sales.
kpis.signal: Strong adoption of digital tools, enhancing customer experience.

kpis.name: Omni Sales
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales where the customer completes at least one step of the purchase process online, but not all four steps.
kpis.description: Indicates CarMax's ability to deliver a seamless buying experience across digital and physical platforms.
kpis.signal: Growth in omnichannel sales, reflecting successful integration of sales channels.

kpis.name: Online Retail Sales
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales where the customer completes all four purchase steps online: reservation, financing, trade-in/decline, and order creation.
kpis.description: Measures the proportion of customers opting for a fully digital buying experience without visiting a store.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in fully online sales, possibly due to a return to mixed purchasing habits.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive sector, with numerous competitors offering competitive pricing and similar services, including new car dealerships with certified pre-owned programs and online sales platforms. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Market Evolution
risks.score_rationale: The used vehicle market is constantly evolving, with technological changes and shifts in consumer behavior. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Economic Conditions
risks.score_rationale: Economic conditions such as recession or inflation could negatively impact the company's sales and results. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Access to Capital
risks.score_rationale: The company requires access to capital to fund its operations and expansion, particularly for CAF. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Reputation
risks.score_rationale: The company's reputation is critical to its success as the nation's largest national retailer of used vehicles.
